about: The definition of rrx-core's reactivity scenarios, run by every library in the benchmark. Graph shapes follow the js-reactivity-benchmark kairo suite. Every write is followed by exactly one propagation: rrx-core calls `$flush` after each write, and libraries with synchronous effects run each write in its own batch. Effects run once when created. A result counts only when sum and runs equal the expected values.
tiers: Every library receives 200 identical warm-up rounds before timing. Node v24.15.0 async traces found background optimization through round 142; 30 warm-ups included tier changes in the timed samples. Repeated processes still measure variability after tier-up.

scenarios.name: deep
scenarios.describe: A chain of `width` memos from one signal, each adding 1 to the previous; one effect reads the tail. The signal is written 1..updates.

scenarios.name: broad
scenarios.describe: `width` memos read the signal, memo i yielding signal + i; each has its own effect. The signal is written 1..updates.

scenarios.name: diamond
scenarios.describe: `width` memos each yield signal + 1; one memo sums them in order; one effect reads the sum. The signal is written 1..updates.

scenarios.name: avoidable
scenarios.describe: A memo reads the signal and always yields 0; a chain of `chain` memos each add 1; one effect reads the tail. Equal-value cutoff keeps the effect from rerunning. The signal is written 1..updates.

scenarios.name: repeated
scenarios.describe: One memo sums `reads` reads of the same signal; one effect reads it. The signal is written 1..updates.

scenarios.name: unstable
scenarios.describe: Signals odd = 1 and even = 2; a memo yields (source % 2 == 0 ? even : odd) + source, so its dependencies switch with the value; one effect reads it. The signal is written 1..updates.

scenarios.name: churn
scenarios.describe: For round in 0..rounds-1: a new owned scope creates `width` pairs of (memo yielding signal + index, effect adding it to the sum); the signal is written round; one propagation; the scope is disposed. Nothing else is disposed until the end.

scenarios.name: disposal
scenarios.describe: `scopes` owned scopes each hold a memo (signal + index), an effect reading it and a cleanup; then every scope is disposed with the library's own ownership primitive, and the signal is written once more (nothing may run). Checksum: cleanups run and effect runs. The worker also reports `blocking`, the time until the last dispose call returned (rrx-retire: `$retire` returns at once and the sweep finishes after).

scenarios.name: async
scenarios.describe: `tasks` async values, task i tracking signal + i; each launch gets a synchronous deferred (resolve), so timing measures the graph, not the event loop. All first launches complete with input*2; then two writes launch twice more, the newer launches complete first and the older ones late with a poison value that must be ignored. Checksum: the sum of the final values and the number of ignored late completions. Libraries without a synchronous async primitive use one generic task (adapters.mjs).

scenarios.name: steps
scenarios.describe: `tasks` async values, task i tracking signal + i and made of `steps` sequential async steps (each adds 1), written the way applications chain requests: an async function awaiting a promise per step. The harness settles the steps in rounds and lets microtasks run between rounds. After every chain's first step the signal changes: the superseded chains are settled last, after every current chain completed, so an accepted late completion changes the sum. Checksum: the sum of the final values and the number of effects that saw a final value.
